confidence_notes: I based the food and drink anchors on web searches. These returned crowdsourced cost-of-living figures for Sharm El Sheikh: cappuccino about $1.8-2.25, domestic beer about $1.4-3.1, inexpensive meal about $4-8 and a three-course mid-range dinner for two about $21.6. One source was last updated in 2023, and these aggregates may lag recent Egyptian price rises. They also understate prices in tourist venues. A current menu found by search for one Naama Bay tourist bar (Camel Bar) listed local 500 ml beer at about EGP 350 and a glass of wine at EGP 480, which is well above the aggregates. A 2026 nightlife guide gave bar beer at EGP 100-250 and cocktails at EGP 200-400. I set beer, cocktail and wine between the aggregates and tourist-venue menus. The cocktail and wine figures rely partly on their usual ratio to beer in local prices and are less certain. I did not verify the EGP/USD rate by search; I used a working assumption of about 48-50 EGP per USD. All four accommodation anchors are estimates from general knowledge only, with no searches or listings checked. Sharm has very few registered hostels, so the dorm and private hostel figures are especially uncertain. July is the hot, lower-demand season, but Russian and regional summer travel keeps rates up. Three-star hotels are often sold as resort or half-board packages. For FX, I could not open the RBA page directly. The 18 November 2026 4pm reading of 0.6720 USD per AUD came from search results, including one limited to rba.gov.au. No 19 November reading was published yet.
comparable_city_reasoning: Resort-priced Egyptian Red Sea destination, comparable to Hurghada with a modest premium, especially in Naama Bay and other tourist areas. Restaurant and bar prices are reported to run well above Egypt's national averages, which are set by Cairo.
